CPP_ASSIGNMENT_IN_IF.message: You used an assignment operator '=' in an if condition; did you mean comparison '=='?
CPP_ASSIGNMENT_IN_IF.description: Using assignment instead of comparison in conditional expressions can make the condition always true or modify variables unexpectedly.
CPP_ASSIGNMENT_IN_IF.remediation: Use == for comparison; if assignment is intended, make it explicit e.g. if ((x = get()) != 0).

CPP_ARRAY_OOB_LITERAL.message: Array accessed with a constant index beyond the declared size.
CPP_ARRAY_OOB_LITERAL.description: A constant index is used to access an array outside its declared range.
CPP_ARRAY_OOB_LITERAL.remediation: Keep indices in [0, size-1]; for an array of length n, valid indices are 0 to n-1.

CPP_ARRAY_OOB_VARIABLE.message: Variable index may be out of bounds; no range check before access.
CPP_ARRAY_OOB_VARIABLE.description: Index is a variable or expression that is not guaranteed to be in [0, size-1] at runtime.
CPP_ARRAY_OOB_VARIABLE.remediation: Check 0 <= index && index < size before access, or use at() for bounds-checked access.

CPP_NULL_POINTER_DEREF.message: Pointer may be nullptr; no null check before dereference.
CPP_NULL_POINTER_DEREF.description: A pointer is dereferenced without ensuring it points to valid memory or is not nullptr.
CPP_NULL_POINTER_DEREF.remediation: Check if (ptr != nullptr) or if (ptr) before dereference; consider smart pointers.

CPP_UNINIT_VAR_USAGE.message: Variable is read before being assigned a definite value.
CPP_UNINIT_VAR_USAGE.description: A local variable is used before it has been given a well-defined initial value.
CPP_UNINIT_VAR_USAGE.remediation: Initialize before use or at declaration, e.g. int x = 0;

CPP_DANGLING_POINTER.message: Pointer used after the pointed-to object has been destroyed or freed.
CPP_DANGLING_POINTER.description: The memory or object the pointer referred to no longer exists; further use is undefined behavior.
CPP_DANGLING_POINTER.remediation: Set ptr = nullptr after delete; or use smart pointers/references to avoid manual lifetime management.

CPP_DOUBLE_FREE.message: Same memory is deleted or freed more than once.
CPP_DOUBLE_FREE.description: The same pointer is freed multiple times, causing undefined behavior and heap corruption.
CPP_DOUBLE_FREE.remediation: Set pointer to nullptr after each delete; or use smart pointers and avoid manual delete.

CPP_USE_AFTER_FREE.message: Memory is accessed through a pointer after it has been freed.
CPP_USE_AFTER_FREE.description: The pointer is used for read or write after delete/free has been called.
CPP_USE_AFTER_FREE.remediation: Do not use the pointer after freeing; reassign it before reuse if needed.

CPP_BUFFER_OVERFLOW.message: Write exceeds buffer bounds and may overwrite adjacent memory.
CPP_BUFFER_OVERFLOW.description: Data is written to an array or fixed-size buffer without checking length, causing out-of-bounds write.
CPP_BUFFER_OVERFLOW.remediation: Use length-bounded APIs (e.g. strncpy, snprintf) or std::string/std::vector.

CPP_STR_NOT_NULL_TERMINATED.message: Character array used as string does not guarantee a trailing '\0'.
CPP_STR_NOT_NULL_TERMINATED.description: When building or copying a string from a char array, a null terminator was not added after the valid content.
CPP_STR_NOT_NULL_TERMINATED.remediation: Ensure a trailing '\0', or use std::string to avoid manual management.

CPP_SWITCH_NO_DEFAULT.message: Switch statement has no default branch; not all possible values are handled.
CPP_SWITCH_NO_DEFAULT.description: Switch does not cover all enum or possible values; missing default can lead to silent bugs.
CPP_SWITCH_NO_DEFAULT.remediation: Add a default branch for unlisted values, or list all cases explicitly.

CPP_MISSING_BREAK.message: A case does not end with break, causing unintended fall-through.
CPP_MISSING_BREAK.description: A switch case does not end with break/return, so execution falls through to the next case.
CPP_MISSING_BREAK.remediation: Add break, return, or [[fallthrough]] at the end of each case to make intent clear.

CPP_NON_VOID_NO_RETURN.message: A function with a return type has a control path that does not execute return.
CPP_NON_VOID_NO_RETURN.description: Some branches do not return a value consistent with the declared return type, leading to undefined behavior.
CPP_NON_VOID_NO_RETURN.remediation: Ensure every path returns a value, or use [[noreturn]] for functions that never return.

CPP_IMPLICIT_NARROWING.message: Implicit type conversion may lose precision or range.
CPP_IMPLICIT_NARROWING.description: e.g. assigning long/double to int causes implicit narrowing and possible truncation or overflow.
CPP_IMPLICIT_NARROWING.remediation: Use explicit static_cast to show intent, or use a larger type and range checks.

CPP_UNSAFE_CAST.message: C-style or reinterpret_cast used in a way that may be unsafe.
CPP_UNSAFE_CAST.description: Inappropriate cast can cause undefined behavior or object slicing.
CPP_UNSAFE_CAST.remediation: Prefer static_cast; use dynamic_cast for polymorphic downcast and check the result.

CPP_VOID_POINTER_USE.display_name: Dereference of void pointer without cast
CPP_VOID_POINTER_USE.message: void* is dereferenced or used in pointer arithmetic without casting to a concrete type.
CPP_VOID_POINTER_USE.description: void* has no type information; direct dereference or pointer arithmetic is invalid.
CPP_VOID_POINTER_USE.remediation: Cast to a concrete pointer type with static_cast before dereferencing.

CPP_UNREACHABLE_CODE.message: Code that can never be executed.
CPP_UNREACHABLE_CODE.description: Code after return/throw or in a branch that is always false is unreachable.
CPP_UNREACHABLE_CODE.remediation: Remove dead code or fix the logic so the branch can be reached.

CPP_INFINITE_LOOP_RISK.message: Loop condition may never become false or loop variable is not updated.
CPP_INFINITE_LOOP_RISK.description: The loop condition does not change, or the loop variable is not updated in the body.
CPP_INFINITE_LOOP_RISK.remediation: Ensure the condition can become false or the loop variable is updated correctly.

CPP_SELF_ASSIGNMENT.display_name: Copy assignment does not check self-assignment
CPP_SELF_ASSIGNMENT.message: operator= does not handle this == &other; self-assignment may corrupt the object.
CPP_SELF_ASSIGNMENT.description: Without a self-assignment check, freeing then copying in operator= can destroy the object.
CPP_SELF_ASSIGNMENT.remediation: Add if (this == &other) return *this; at the start of operator=.

CPP_VIRTUAL_DESTRUCTOR_MISSING.display_name: Polymorphic base class without virtual destructor
CPP_VIRTUAL_DESTRUCTOR_MISSING.message: Deleting a derived object via base pointer with non-virtual destructor is undefined behavior.
CPP_VIRTUAL_DESTRUCTOR_MISSING.description: If the base destructor is not virtual, delete via base pointer will not call the derived destructor.
CPP_VIRTUAL_DESTRUCTOR_MISSING.remediation: Declare the destructor virtual if the class is used as a polymorphic base.

CPP_ITERATOR_INVALIDATION.message: Iterator is used after the container was modified; it may be invalid.
CPP_ITERATOR_INVALIDATION.description: After insert/erase/push_back etc., iterators may be invalidated; using them is undefined behavior.
CPP_ITERATOR_INVALIDATION.remediation: Re-obtain iterators after modifying the container, or use indices; check the documentation for invalidation rules.

CPP_RESERVED_IDENTIFIER.message: Identifier starts with underscore or contains double underscore; reserved for the implementation.
CPP_RESERVED_IDENTIFIER.description: Identifiers starting with _ or containing __ are reserved and may conflict with the implementation.
CPP_RESERVED_IDENTIFIER.remediation: Avoid leading underscore and __ in identifiers.

CPP_DIVISION_BY_ZERO.message: Divisor may be zero; no check before division or modulo.
CPP_DIVISION_BY_ZERO.description: In / or % the divisor may be 0, causing undefined behavior or exception.
CPP_DIVISION_BY_ZERO.remediation: Check divisor != 0 before division, or use conditional logic to avoid division by zero.

CPP_UNINIT_MEMBER.message: Class member may be used before being initialized in the constructor.
CPP_UNINIT_MEMBER.description: Constructor does not initialize all members or the initializer list omits some.
CPP_UNINIT_MEMBER.remediation: Initialize all members in the constructor initializer list or give default values.

CPP_RECURSION_NO_BASE.message: Recursive function may not return on a boundary condition, leading to infinite recursion.
CPP_RECURSION_NO_BASE.description: Not all paths provide a base case, which can cause stack overflow.
CPP_RECURSION_NO_BASE.remediation: Handle the base case first and return; then handle the recursive case.

CPP_NEGATIVE_INDEX.message: A negative value is used as array or container index.
CPP_NEGATIVE_INDEX.description: A negative index accesses memory before the array; severe out-of-bounds access.
CPP_NEGATIVE_INDEX.remediation: Ensure index is non-negative; if computed, check index >= 0 before use.
